title: The Catalan-triangle recurrence B(p,q) = B(p−1,q) + B(p,q−1) from the ballot closed form and Pascal's rule

problemStatement.formal:
The parent entry catalan-numbers-oq-01-oq-01-oq-02 proves the ballot closed form B(p,q) = C(p+q,q) − C(p+q,p+1) and asks (openQuestions[2]) to derive the Catalan-triangle recurrence B(p,q) = B(p−1,q) + B(p,q−1) (for q ≤ p) directly from that closed form and Pascal's rule, exhibiting the full triangle structure.

**Answer:** ballot_recurrence establishes exactly this for 1 ≤ q ≤ p, and ballot_recurrence_diag specializes it to the diagonal edge rule ballot n n = ballot n (n−1).
problemStatement.plain: Answers the parent entry's lead open question: derive the defining two-term recurrence of the Catalan triangle, ballot p q = ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1) for 1 ≤ q ≤ p, directly from the parent's closed form ballot p q = C(p+q,q) − C(p+q,p+1) and Pascal's rule. The proof is pure binomial algebra: substituting p = a+1, q = b+1 makes every binomial index a clean polynomial in a,b; Pascal's rule Nat.choose_succ_succ' splits each of the two binomials of ballot p q into the two reduced-row coefficients; and the parent's ballot_genuine supplies the three genuineness bounds (C(p+q,p+1) ≤ C(p+q,q) and its shifts) that let the truncated ℕ-subtractions recombine — a single omega then closes the goal over the six binomial atoms. As a corollary, the diagonal recurrence ballot n n = ballot n (n−1) follows because the left neighbour ballot (n−1) n lies above the diagonal and vanishes (parent's ballot_eq_zero_of_lt). Together with the boundary ballot p 0 = 1, the recurrence regenerates the entire Catalan triangle row by row. Verified with 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide.

proven: ballot_recurrence: ballot p q = ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1) for 1 ≤ q ≤ p — the defining additive law of the Catalan triangle, derived directly from the parent's closed form and Pascal's rule (this is the parent entry's lead open question openQuestions[2]).

Proof technique: substitute p = a+1, q = b+1 to clear the predecessors and normalise indices; apply Pascal's rule Nat.choose_succ_succ' to each of the two binomials of ballot p q; supply three genuineness bounds from the parent's ballot_genuine (covering the diagonal edge q = p as an equality); then close the linear ℕ-relation among the six binomial coefficients with a single omega — no path counting, no real-valued probability.

ballot_recurrence_diag: ballot n n = ballot n (n−1) for n ≥ 1 — the edge rule carrying the Catalan numbers up the diagonal, since the left neighbour ballot (n−1) n vanishes above the diagonal (parent's ballot_eq_zero_of_lt).
Three concrete kernel-decide sanity checks of the recurrence: B(4,2) = B(3,2) + B(4,1) (9 = 5+4), the diagonal B(3,3) = B(3,2) (5 = 5), and B(5,3) = B(4,3) + B(5,2).

insights: **The recurrence is Pascal's rule, reflected.** ballot p q = C(p+q,q) − C(p+q,p+1) is a difference of two binomials; applying Pascal's rule to each and regrouping yields exactly ballot (p−1) q + ballot p (q−1). The Catalan-triangle recurrence is the difference of two copies of Pascal's recurrence.

**Clearing predecessors removes all truncated subtraction from the indices.** Writing p = a+1, q = b+1 turns p−1, q−1, p+1 into honest sums a, b, a+2, so Pascal's rule and the genuineness lemma apply on the nose and omega never has to reason about index truncation — only about the value-level subtractions, which the genuineness bounds make exact.

**The diagonal edge is the recurrence with a vanishing neighbour.** On the diagonal the left neighbour ballot (n−1) n sits strictly above the diagonal of its own row and is 0, so B(n,n) = B(n,n−1): the rule that propagates catalan n = B(n,n) up the triangle's edge is a special case of the two-term recurrence, not a separate fact.

**Genuineness covers the diagonal as an equality.** The one bound not directly furnished by ballot_genuine (the q = p case of the left neighbour) holds because the two binomial indices coincide there — the proof splits b < a (Pascal genuineness) from b = a (reflexivity), so the single omega works uniformly across the closed regime 1 ≤ q ≤ p.
